name: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in Caucasians and African Americans

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of large neoplastic B cells with diffuse growth pattern on lymph node biopsy
Expression of B-cell markers CD19, CD20, CD22, and variable expression of BCL6 and MUM1
Detection of rearrangements involving BCL2, BCL6, or MYC genes by FISH or PCR
Rapidly enlarging lymphadenopathy or extranodal mass with B symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of diffuse large B-cell proliferation with supportive immunophenotyping
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies aid in subclassification and prognosis but are not mandatory for diagnosis

searchTerms: fast growing painless swollen lymph nodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: B symptoms (fever >38°C, night sweats, weight loss >10%)
searchTerms: fever, night sweats, and weight loss
classic systemic symptoms including fever and sweating
B symptoms like fever and weight loss

common.symptomName: Extranodal mass causing local compressive symptoms
common.notes: Common sites include gastrointestinal tract, CNS, and bone

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to anemia of chronic disease
searchTerms: fatigue due to low red blood cells
weakness from anemia of chronic disease

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow involvement
searchTerms: aching bones due to marrow disease
neurological deficits from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to CNS disease
weakness or sensory loss from CNS

occasional.symptomName: Pleural effusion secondary to thoracic involvement
Skin lesions from cutaneous lymphoma involvement
searchTerms: skin bumps or rashes from lymphoma

rare.symptomName: Paraneoplastic syndromes such as hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
searchTerms: immune system overactivation related to cancer

rare.symptomName: Superior vena cava syndrome due to mediastinal mass
searchTerms: swelling from superior vena cava blockage
face and neck swelling from chest mass
renal impairment due to tumor infiltration

imaging: CT/PET showing bulky lymphadenopathy and extranodal masses
genetic: BCL2, BCL6, and MYC gene rearrangements
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD19, CD20, CD22

distinguishingFeatures: MYC translocation as primary genetic event

redFlags: Rapidly progressive lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms
Unexplained persistent fevers and night sweats
New onset neurological deficits in lymphoma patient
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Non-Hodgkin's Lymphomas, Version 6.2023.
Armitage JO. Treatment of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. N Engl J Med. 2013;369(7):675-7.
